t: The Luba Empire was a sacred kingship centred on the Upemba Depression in what is now south-eastern DR Congo.
Its model of royal power, checked by the Bambudye society, was copied by neighbours such as the Lunda across the southern savanna.
A succession war after c. 1870, slave raiding and Congo Free State conquest in the 1890s ended its independence.
dyk: Luba historians kept royal memory on the lukasa, a hand-held beaded board whose patterns of beads and shells helped Bambudye adepts recall kings, places and lineages.
